author: cli
text: Re-read 2026-08-17. The resolution-provenance paragraph is if anything more load-bearing than when written: runtime-recorded edges from probe still carry their own resolution marker, and 0.55.5 added a second reason a reader must not assume the graph is complete - unresolved_refs on before_edit. Both say the same thing from different ends: a reader who cannot tell how an edge was established will assume the source says what the graph says.

author: cli
text:
Re-read after the payload census. Every earlier claim still holds: the resolution/confidence fields still exist so a reader can tell a runtime edge from a static one, and lineage resolution is unchanged.

What changed: the edge list is RANKED, BOUNDED and REPORTED through payload.rank_bound_report. show on DirLocker.Lock in prometheus was 55,829 characters of which 55,572 was a single 344-entry edges list - 99.5% of the payload, one field. Now 2,293 (-96%).

The ORDER is what makes the cut survivable, and it is deliberate: OUT edges first, because what an entity calls describes the entity and there are always far fewer of them than callers; then production before tests; then confidence descending, so a bare-name guess can never displace an exact edge in the twelve you see. edges_total and edges_shown ride alongside, so a reader knows 12 of 344 rather than believing they saw the neighbourhood.
